name: aimonitor
description: See every AI process, token, and account limit on your machine, inside VSCode. Runs fully offline.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Reads only its own bundled files and your local Claude usage data. It never reads or runs workspace code.

aimon.pythonPath.markdownDescription:
Python interpreter used to run the AI Monitor server. Filled in automatically the first time the extension runs; clear it to go back to detecting one every time. A path that stops working is detected and replaced on the next start, so this never leaves you stuck.

[$(search) Detect again](command:aimon.selectPython)

aimon.serverPort.markdownDescription: Port for the local server. `0` lets the operating system pick a free one, which is what you want unless a firewall rule needs a fixed port.

aimon.reuseRunningInstance.markdownDescription: Reuse an AI Monitor server that is already running - the standalone app, or another VSCode window - instead of starting a second one. Turn this off to always get a private server for this window.

enumDescriptions: Open the full dashboard as an editor tab
Reveal the dashboard in the activity bar panel
aimon.openIn.markdownDescription: What the status bar item opens. The editor tab is the full-width dashboard; the activity bar panel is a compact version made for a narrow column.

aimon.statusBar.enabled.markdownDescription: Show AI Monitor in the status bar at the bottom of the window.

aimon.statusBar.metric.markdownDescription: What the status bar item shows while a server is running.

aimon.statusBar.alignment.markdownDescription: Which side of the status bar to sit on. Takes effect after the window is reloaded.

aimon.refreshSeconds.markdownDescription: How often the dashboard refreshes, in seconds. Raise it on a busy machine - each refresh lists every running process.

aimon.claudeDataDir.markdownDescription:
Folder holding your Claude Code data. Filled in automatically the first time the extension runs; empty means `~/.claude`. Only applies to a server this extension starts itself.

[$(search) Detect again](command:aimon.selectClaudeDir)

aimon.pricingFile.markdownDescription:
Token price table used to work out cost. Filled in automatically the first time the extension runs; empty means the `pricing.json` bundled with the extension. The bundled path changes on every extension update and is refreshed for you. Only applies to a server this extension starts itself.

[$(search) Detect again](command:aimon.selectPricingFile)

aimon.aiKinds.markdownDescription:
Which kinds of AI agent the dashboard and the Office view start out showing. Most machines run background processes that get classified as AI without you ever launching them - Copilot helpers, editor-bundled Codex - and showing all of them buries the sessions you actually care about.

This is a starting point, not a lock: the **Show:** row at the top of the dashboard turns each kind on and off, and what you pick there wins and is remembered.

enumDescriptions: Voyage - thirty-six sailors, hats, goggles and beards
Ninja - thirty-six shinobi, headbands, masks and cloaks
Office - ten people, different hair and outfits
Pets - cat, dog, rabbit, sheep, cow, pig, chick, duckling, frog
Mascots - ten round mascots, each with its own hat
The Crew - five friends, told apart by hair, glasses and outfit
aimon.officePack.markdownDescription:
Character set used in the Office view. Every agent gets a *different* character from the set; once the set runs out it starts over.

This is a starting point, not a lock: **Character set** under the room shows each set with a preview, and clicking a character in the room changes just that one. What you pick there wins and is remembered.
